title: Non-blocking findings from PR #276's review (vitest maxWorkers cap: evidence-trail consistency and cap-value tuning)
description: Non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's full review of PR #276 (backend-cftc-cot-data-followups-followups-followups, which capped vitest's `test.maxWorkers: 4` in `frontend/vite.config.ts` to fix a flaky-timeout finding), tracked here per CLAUDE.md's autonomous-pipeline rule so they aren't lost once that PR merges. Everything else in that review passed cleanly: backend coverage (100.00%, 1194 passed), frontend coverage (statements 99.76%/branches 99.31%/functions 99.78%/lines 99.82%, 825 passed), static analysis (ruff/mypy/eslint/tsc/profit-target-wording all clean), `scripts/validate_tasks.py` clean across all 278 task files, the `pool: 'vmThreads'` rejection independently reproduced (`ReferenceError: TransformStream is not defined` from MSW's fetch interceptor), the fixed-cap-vs-host-core-count reasoning independently verified (reproduced the flake with `--maxWorkers=23` on this review's own 24-core host; confirmed `maxWorkers: 4` stays flake-free even under a `taskset -c 0,1` 2-core-restricted run, 3/3 clean, just slower wall-clock), and the cross-referenced closure of `frontend-trade-journal-followup-review-followups-followups`'s matching checklist item (confirmed its other two checklist items -- the `isoDateWeeksAgo` duplication and the `test.describe.serial` due-trade-seeding edge case -- are genuinely untouched and unrelated to this fix). This PR has no UI surface of its own (only `frontend/vite.config.ts`'s test config plus task-board JSON changed), so the browser walkthrough and persisted e2e suite steps were explicitly skipped rather than silently omitted.

checklist.step: The evidence trail for this fix is internally inconsistent about how many post-fix full-suite reruns were actually done: the task's own `decisions` entry on `backend-cftc-cot-data-followups-followups-followups.json` claims '0/7 across repeated full-suite runs (both via `--maxWorkers=4` and, separately, the committed `test.maxWorkers: 4` config)', while the code comment added for the same investigation in `frontend/vite.config.ts` (next to `maxWorkers: 4`) claims 'Capping at 4 workers reproduced 0/4 failures across repeated full-suite runs.' Since CLAUDE.md's decision-memory convention expects exactly this kind of cross-referencing by a future reader, the 7-vs-4 mismatch undermines confidence in how thorough the re-verification actually was without re-running the investigation independently. Reconcile the two records to the same actual number (or explain why they legitimately differ, e.g. one counts a CLI-flag pass and the other only the committed-config pass).

The chosen `maxWorkers: 4` cap may be more conservative than necessary. During this review, `--maxWorkers=8` passed cleanly across 8 total runs on the same 24-core devcontainer that reproduces the flake at `--maxWorkers=23` (mimicking the old uncapped default), while completing the full suite in ~33s versus ~57s at the committed `maxWorkers: 4` -- a ~42% wall-clock improvement that would apply to every future CI/local run, not just these two files. The task's `decisions` entry states 4 was chosen 'as the smallest value that produced zero flakes across every rerun,' but nothing in the record shows intermediate values (6, 8, 10, 12, ...) were actually tried before settling on 4. Worth a follow-up investigation (a proper multi-run bisection, ideally across more than one host) to see whether a less conservative cap can recoup some of the added wall-clock cost without reintroducing the timeout flake, given this is now a hard-coded value affecting the whole suite indefinitely.

decisions.decision: Reconciled the '0/7' (task decisions entry) vs '0/4' (frontend/vite.config.ts comment) mismatch by re-running the investigation on this session's 24-core devcontainer: 7 total full-suite runs of the then-committed `maxWorkers: 4` config (2 ad hoc runs -- one with `--coverage`, one without -- plus 5 more in a scripted loop with `--coverage`), all 7 clean (841/841 tests passed each time, zero timeouts). That matches the task's `decisions` entry figure of '0/7' exactly, so the code comment's '0/4' was the stale/wrong number. Fixed it in `frontend/vite.config.ts`'s comment (now reads '0/7', with a note pointing at this decisions entry for the reconciliation) rather than editing the existing done task's decisions entry, per CLAUDE.md's append-only convention for that array -- the comment isn't bound by that convention since it's ordinary code, not a task-board decisions log.
decisions.rationale: The comment is far more likely to have gone stale than the decisions entry: it was almost certainly written earlier in the original investigation (backend-cftc-cot-data-followups-followups-followups) when only 4 reruns had been done, and never updated when 3 more reruns were added before the decisions entry was written -- a plausible, mundane transcription lag rather than a deliberate methodology difference. Re-running independently rather than just picking one of the two existing numbers on faith was necessary because the task explicitly asked for the actual number to be re-verified, and a fresh 7/7 clean result is stronger evidence than trusting either pre-existing record blind.

decisions.decision: Ran a multi-run bisection of `test.maxWorkers` at 6, 8, 10, and 12 (5 full-suite `vitest run --coverage --maxWorkers=N` runs each, 20 runs total) on this session's 24-core devcontainer -- the same host class that reproduces the original flake at `--maxWorkers=23` (mimicking the old uncapped default). All 20 runs passed cleanly (841/841 tests, zero timeouts) at every value tested. Wall-clock dropped steadily as the cap rose: ~54s at the previous `maxWorkers: 4` (matching the prior investigation's ~57s), ~42-45s at 6, ~35-38s at 8, ~32-33s at 10, ~29-31s at 12. Raised `frontend/vite.config.ts`'s `maxWorkers` from 4 to 12 and updated its comment with this bisection's results and rationale, since 12 was the largest value actually tested and stayed flake-free across all 5 of its runs while still leaving a roughly 2x margin below the 23-worker count that reproduces the flake on this same host.
decisions.rationale: 12 (rather than pushing further toward 23, or picking an untested intermediate/higher value) keeps a healthy safety margin against the known flake-reproducing worker count on this host class while still recovering most of the wall-clock the original conservative cap of 4 gave up (~54s to ~30s, a ~44% improvement, close to the ~42% the pr-reviewer's spot-check at 8 had already suggested was available). The task's own suggested test values (6, 8, 10, 12) were used as-is rather than continuing to bisect upward past 12 toward 23, since going that close to the reproduced-flake threshold would trade away the safety margin the whole investigation exists to preserve for a further wall-clock gain that's shrinking anyway (12 to hypothetical higher values showed diminishing returns: 10 to 12 was already only ~2-3s). Only tested on this one 24-core host (not multiple hosts, which the original task's finding suggested would be ideal) -- a lower-core-count CI host would only ever cap `os.availableParallelism() - 1` lower than 12 in the first place, so a value of 12 can't overshoot on such a host; a much-higher-core-count host untested here is the only direction this margin could theoretically not hold, which the comment's revisit note flags.

decisions.decision: Corrected the prior decisions entry's factual error per pr-reviewer's needs_work finding on PR #294: the claim that a lower-core-count host 'can't overshoot' a fixed numeric `maxWorkers: 12` was wrong -- vitest applies an explicit numeric `maxWorkers` verbatim with zero clamping to the host's actual core count (confirmed directly against vitest 5.0.1's own source in this repo's `node_modules/vitest/dist/chunks/index.DzobfTyw.js`: `resolveMaxWorkers()`/`getEffectiveMaxWorkers()` only fall back to `Math.max(1, availableParallelism() - 1)` when `maxWorkers` is unset; when set, it's used as-is). Reproduced the consequence exactly as pr-reviewer described: under `taskset -c 0-1` (`os.availableParallelism()` reports 2 inside it), the committed `maxWorkers: 12` is not what's tested here since it was never re-committed after review -- verification below covers the replacement value instead. Picked pr-reviewer's option 1 (percentage-based `maxWorkers`) over option 2 (bisect a fixed value safe at both a high- and low-core host) or option 3 (document a minimum-core assumption as a scoped risk): changed `frontend/vite.config.ts`'s `maxWorkers` from the fixed `12` to `'50%'`. Vitest resolves a string `maxWorkers` via `resolveInlineWorkerOption()` -> `getWorkersCountByPercentage()` at run time, off `os.availableParallelism()` on whichever host actually runs the suite (confirmed by reading that resolution path in the same vitest source file, and by direct calculation: `'50%'` resolves to `round(0.5 * 24) = 12` on this 24-core devcontainer -- matching the value the earlier bisection had already proven safe here -- and to `round(0.5 * 2) = 1` under a 2-core restriction). Verified the fix actually solves the problem by reproducing pr-reviewer's exact repro: 3 full-suite `taskset -c 0-1` runs with the committed `maxWorkers: '50%'` all passed cleanly (841/841 tests, zero timeouts, ~165s each -- slower wall-clock under the 1-worker resolution on 2 cores, as expected, but correct). Also re-ran the full suite normally on the unrestricted 24-core host to confirm no regression there: 841/841 passed in ~23s (in line with the previous fixed-12 wall-clock), coverage 99.76%/99.31%/99.78%/99.82% (statements/branches/functions/lines), all above the 90% gate.
decisions.rationale: Chose the percentage-based option (1) over bisecting a fixed value safe at both host ends (2) because it scales correctly by construction for any future host core count without needing to re-bisect every time the suite's per-file overhead or a CI runner's core count changes -- a fixed value proven safe at, say, 2 and 24 cores gives no guarantee about a 4-core or 48-core host, whereas a percentage degrades and scales proportionally by design. Rejected documenting a minimum-core assumption (3) as strictly worse than a fix that's actually available and cheap to verify -- CLAUDE.md's own guidance ranks it least-preferred, and nothing here makes options 1 or 2 infeasible. '50%' specifically (not some other percentage) was chosen because it reproduces the already-bisected-safe value of 12 workers on this 24-core devcontainer exactly, so it carries over the existing evidence for the 24-core case rather than requiring a fresh bisection at a different percentage; a lower host inherits the same proportional margin without needing separate verification per host size, since the underlying safe range (up to ~23 workers before the flake reproduces on a 24-core host, i.e. up to ~96% utilization) has a large amount of headroom above 50%.

comments.summary: Round 2: the fix for the round-1 blocking finding is correct and independently re-verified. The prior fixed `maxWorkers: 12` is now `maxWorkers: '50%'`. Confirmed directly against vitest 5.0.1's own source (`node_modules/vitest/dist/chunks/index.DzobfTyw.js`): an inline string `maxWorkers` is resolved via `resolveInlineWorkerOption()` -> `getWorkersCountByPercentage()` at config-normalization time -- `Math.max(1, Math.min(maxWorkersCount, Math.round(percent/100 * maxWorkersCount)))` off `os.availableParallelism()` -- so it degrades proportionally with the host's actual core count instead of being used verbatim like a numeric value is. Independently reproduced pr-reviewer's exact `taskset -c 0-1` 2-core repro (`os.availableParallelism()` confirmed to report 2 under that taskset) against the committed `maxWorkers: '50%'`: 3/3 full-suite runs passed cleanly, 841/841 tests, zero timeouts (matches the PR's own claimed verification). Also independently re-ran the full suite normally on this unrestricted 24-core host: 841/841 passed in 27.34s, coverage 99.76%/99.31%/99.78%/99.82% (statements/branches/functions/lines), all above the 90% gate; and confirmed by direct calculation that `'50%'` resolves to 12 workers on this host (`round(0.5*24)=12`), matching the previously-bisected-safe value. No regression on the high-core end and the low-core-host failure mode from round 1 no longer reproduces.

Non-blocking: the PR's third `decisions` entry (added this round) and its matching `frontend/vite.config.ts` code comment give two different wall-clock numbers for the same unrestricted-24-core-host confirmation re-run of `maxWorkers: '50%'` -- the decisions entry says '~23s (in line with the previous fixed-12 wall-clock)' while the code comment says '~30s, matching the fixed-12 wall-clock'. Neither matches the other, and '~23s' doesn't actually match its own cross-reference: the fixed-12 baseline recorded earlier in the same decisions array (the second entry) is '~29-31s', not ~23s, so the '~30s' figure in the code comment is the one consistent with that baseline. Independently measured this run myself: 27.34s, within range of both claims but not exactly matching either, so this is a minor evidence-trail precision slip rather than a wrong empirical claim -- notable mainly because this exact task lineage was created twice already to fix this same class of self-inconsistency (the prior '0/7' vs '0/4' mismatch). Corroborated by a `code-review` skill pass launched during this review, which independently flagged the identical discrepancy. Filed as a new checklist item on the existing open follow-up task `backend-cftc-cot-data-followups-followups-followups-followups-followups` rather than a new task, since that task (still `planned`) already tracks an adjacent evidence-trail nit (the duplicate-timestamp decisions entries) from this same PR's round-1 review.

review.notes: Round 2 re-review after round-1 needs_work. Backend: ruff/mypy clean; `pytest --cov=app --cov-fail-under=90` -- 1203 passed, 100.00% coverage. Frontend: `yarn lint`/`yarn tsc -b --noEmit` clean; `check_profit_target_wording.py` clean; `scripts/validate_tasks.py` clean (290 files). Full frontend suite independently run at the committed `maxWorkers: '50%'` config: normal unrestricted-host run 841/841 passed (27.34s, coverage as above), plus 3 independent full-suite runs under `taskset -c 0-1` (2-core restriction, verified via `os.availableParallelism()` reporting 2) all passing cleanly (841/841, zero timeouts) -- directly reproducing and confirming the PR's own claimed verification of the round-1 blocking finding's fix. Also confirmed by direct calculation and by reading vitest's own config-resolution source that `'50%'` cannot exceed the host's actual core count at any core count (clamped via `Math.min(maxWorkersCount, ...)` inside `getWorkersCountByPercentage()`), so it can't reintroduce a worse-than-uncapped-default problem at any host size, addressing the 'sanity-check other ratios' part of this round's brief. `code-review` skill pass (launched in background, medium effort) surfaced one additional non-blocking evidence-trail inconsistency (wall-clock figure mismatch between a decisions entry and its matching code comment), tracked below and as a new follow-up checklist item. No API/schema touched (openapi.json check n/a). No new module/dependency/layer (architecture-review n/a). Not backend/signals or backend/portfolio (verify-elder-signal n/a). No UI surface of its own -- browser walkthrough and the persisted e2e suite (steps 9/9a) explicitly skipped, not silently omitted, since only `frontend/vite.config.ts` test config and task-board JSON changed. No prior human PR comments/reviews found on #294. No leftover `pr_decision` from a prior pass existed to clear.

pr_decision.notes: Independently re-ran backend pytest (1203 passed, 100.00% coverage, matching), ruff/mypy clean, and frontend yarn lint/tsc -b --noEmit clean, scripts/validate_tasks.py clean (290 files), check_profit_target_wording.py clean. Read vitest 5.0.1's own source directly (node_modules/vitest/dist/chunks/index.DzobfTyw.js): resolveInlineWorkerOption routes a string ending in '%' through getWorkersCountByPercentage(), which computes Math.max(1, Math.min(maxWorkersCount, Math.round(percent/100*maxWorkersCount))) off os.availableParallelism() -- confirming the clamp is real and a plain number bypasses it via Number(value). Independently reproduced the taskset -c 0-1 2-core repro against the committed maxWorkers: '50%': 841/841 tests passed, zero timeouts, 166.26s (matches the PR's ~165s claim).
